observations: White DSLR camera body with a lens attached.
The lens has a black cap with 'Canon' printed on it.
The camera body has 'Canon' branding on the top left and 'EOS 100D' on the top right in photo 2.
The rear LCD screen is visible in photo 1, but it is dark and shows reflections.
The camera is being held by a person's hand in all photos.
Watermark 'CDICSON BUSINESS WORLD' appears on all photos.

claims.evidence: The model name is clearly printed on the camera body in photo 2.
This is a general description of the model; the photos cannot confirm the megapixel count or the physical size.

risks.risk: The camera may not power on or the LCD screen may be dead.
risks.proof: A video showing the camera powering on and the LCD screen displaying a menu or image.

risks.risk: The lens may be a third-party clone rather than the original Canon kit lens.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the lens barrel showing the brand name and model number.

risks.risk: The shutter may be near the end of its life (high shutter count).
risks.proof: A screenshot of a shutter count utility showing the total actuations.

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on and the LCD screen working.
Photo of the lens barrel showing the brand and model.
response.reason: The model is clearly identified from the photos, so it can be priced at its worst case as a non-working unit.
